advice: Experiment: change only the n=512 wrapper and the SME consumer’s B access so gemm packs B into K-major panels before computing. Keep packing and allocation inside gemm, and include both in the timed call. Use unchanged FP32 values and the same accumulation order. Compare against the current source with paired controls. Hypothesis: panel layout may make B loads for the SME tiles more local or simpler; packing may instead cost more than it saves. This is unverified advice, not a measured fact.
risks: Packing adds a full matrix read, write, and allocation per call, so total time may increase. Panel indexing or edge handling could corrupt results. Retain the existing fallback and BSD 3-Clause notice. Check n=512 against tolerance 0.002, test general sizes and odd tails, verify n<=0 behavior, and measure repeated candidate and unchanged-control scores under the fixed benchmark. Do not infer a cause from noisy scores or attribute a joint result to this proposal alone.
